response.summary: Evidence: current keys collide on separators, commit is non-atomic, sequence is per Orders instance, and publisher lacks ownership/expiry checks. Design: retain existing exported classes; make Store the authoritative atomic, copy-isolated, globally sequenced state owner, with collision-free tuple keys/IDs and Publisher transition guards.
plan: Replace delimiter-concatenated identity with an injective encoding of the exact (customer, requestId) tuple; use it consistently for order lookup and event IDs so separators cannot collide.

Validate nonempty primitive-string customer/requestId/sku/worker identifiers, positive integer quantity and leaseMs, and applicable finite time/token inputs before mutation; reject invalid submissions without records.

In Orders.submit, validate replay payload against an existing customer-scoped order: identical sku and quantity returns a fresh snapshot regardless of now; differing sku or quantity throws conflict; same requestId for another customer is independent.

Move successful event sequence allocation to Store.commit, assigning it only as part of a successful pair commit. Commit must check simulated event failure before changing either map, consume that failure flag, and then write copied order/event together; retry therefore creates exactly one pair.
Keep every Store read and mutation boundary copy-isolated: findOrder, getEvent, listEvents, commit inputs, replaceEvent inputs, and Orders/Pubisher return values must not expose stored references.

Have Publisher.claim first resolve expired leases: a lease at its maximum consumed attempt becomes dead; otherwise it is eligible for replacement. Select across all events by dueAt then Store-assigned successful-commit sequence, claim only pending/retry due events or eligible expired leases, and atomically issue a new token, owner, leaseUntil, and incremented attempt.

Require ack and retry to target a currently leased event with exactly matching worker and token. Ack marks sent without time-based expiry rejection; retry clears lease ownership, schedules dueAt by retryDelay, and marks dead instead when the consumed attempt reaches maxAttempts.

Make cancel succeed only for nonterminal events, transition to cancelled and clear/invalidate any live lease; sent, dead, and cancelled events are terminal and neither claimable nor cancellable. response.summary: Inspected TASK.md and all five src files. Evidence: identity ignores customer or uses ambiguous separators (src/keys.ts:1-2); replay bypasses validation and sequence is instance-local (src/orders.ts:6-12); commit writes an order before simulated failure (src/store.ts:24-28); claims ignore expired leases and ownership checks are absent (src/publisher.ts:9-40). Proposed repair: retain exported classes and synchronous APIs, centralize atomic storage and sequence allocation, and enforce an explicit lease state machine. Numeric clock validation and direct Store mutation safeguards below are defensive design inferences, not additional stated acceptance criteria.
plan: In src/keys.ts:1-2, encode the exact customer/requestId tuple using JSON.stringify([customer, requestId]); prefix that encoding for event IDs if desired. Never split identifiers on separators, trim them, or coerce them. Distinct tuples must remain distinct even with separator-containing identifiers.

In src/types.ts:27-28, reuse isIdentifier for every public identifier input, including worker and event IDs. In src/orders.ts:9-12, validate customer, requestId, sku and positive integer quantity before replay lookup. Validate supplied clocks as finite numbers, leaseMs as a positive integer, and ownership tokens as positive safe integers before mutations; reject nonfinite computed deadlines. Malformed inputs must not alter records or allocate sequences. Preserve existing throw-style validation for submit/claim and use false for invalid ack/retry/cancel requests.

In src/orders.ts:10-22, replay only when both sku and quantity exactly match the stored customer-scoped order; otherwise throw a conflict. Ignore valid now differences when comparing replay payloads and preserve original createdAt. Another customer using the same requestId creates a separate pair. Replays must neither commit nor consume an injected event failure.

In src/store.ts:24-29, validate and copy both candidate records before touching maps: matching customer/request identity, canonical event ID, kind order.submitted, valid order fields and initial event fields. Reject duplicate order keys or event IDs rather than overwriting either existing record. Check and consume failEvent only at the event-write stage of an otherwise valid new commit, throwing before either map changes. A failed commit must preserve every pre-existing record and both counts; retry must insert exactly one pair.

Move sequence allocation from src/orders.ts:6,19 into Store in src/store.ts:7-10,24-29. Assign the next store-wide sequence to the staged event, publish both staged records synchronously with no remaining validation or injected failure point, then advance the counter. Caller-provided sequence values must not control ordering; failure and replay consume no sequence. Preserve existing class exports and public method signatures.

In src/orders.ts:13-23 and src/store.ts:4-5,15-33, keep only private copies and return detached order/event objects and list arrays. Flat primitive-valued records in src/types.ts:1-24 make shallow copies sufficient. Copy inputs on commit/replaceEvent, validate replacement before writing, and protect immutable event identity, customer/request linkage, kind and committed sequence. Publisher returns must also be detached; mutating any returned record or list must never change stored state.

In src/publisher.ts:9-18, validate the entire claim request before processing events. Eligible events are pending with dueAt <= now and leased with leaseUntil <= now; retry remains represented by pending in src/types.ts:9. Sweep exhausted eligible events to dead, clearing lease ownership, and exclude them from selection. Sort remaining eligible candidates by dueAt and then Store-assigned sequence across all Orders instances. Preserve dueAt on lease acquisition/reclamation so it remains the ordering key.

For every successful claim in src/publisher.ts:15-17, require attempts < maxAttempts, increment attempts and the event-local monotonic token exactly once, set state leased, leaseOwner to worker and leaseUntil to now + leaseMs. Expired nonfinal leases can be replaced even by the same worker but always receive a fresh token. A final expired lease becomes dead during claim processing rather than receiving another attempt; terminalization must not prevent claiming another eligible event.

In src/publisher.ts:21-27, ack succeeds only for a leased event with exact current worker and token, then marks sent and clears lease metadata. Do not compare wall-clock time: an otherwise unchanged expired lease remains acknowledgeable until claim processing replaces or terminalizes it. Pending, missing, terminal and stale-owner/token requests return false without mutation.

In src/publisher.ts:29-36, retry requires the same current leased owner/token checks and validates now before mutation. If attempts >= maxAttempts, mark dead; otherwise mark pending with dueAt = now + retryDelay. Clear lease metadata in either case. Retry itself does not increment attempts or create a new claim token; the next successful claim does both. Duplicate retries, stale tokens and acknowledgements after retry fail because the event is no longer leased.

In src/publisher.ts:38-43, cancel accepts pending or leased events, marks cancelled and clears lease metadata, immediately invalidating any active ownership. Missing, sent, dead and already-cancelled events return false unchanged. Treat sent/dead/cancelled as absorbing states across claim, ack, retry, cancel and Store replacement safeguards.

response.summary: Evidence: TASK.md requires atomic failure behavior, receipt-based idempotency returning the immutable creation response, exact terminal/expiry rules, conservation, and deep detachment. Current service checks current version before receipts, returns the live hold on retry, mutates on insufficient stock, expires only for expiresAt < now, and treats opposite terminal transitions as false; Store shallow-copies receipt.result. Inference/design: preserve all APIs while making policy pure validation/transition calculations, Store the detached-state boundary, and Reservations the ordered orchestration boundary.
plan: Store: deep-copy Receipt.request and Receipt.result in constructor-adjacent storage paths, receipt(), snapshot(), and commit(); retain detached copies for item/hold/pending and ensure commit never retains nested caller references. Invariant: no getter, constructor input, commit input, or hold response can mutate internal state.

Policy: validate all hold request fields (nonempty id/sku; positive safe count/life; nonnegative safe expected/now; safe now+life) before mutation. Include life in sameRequest identity. Invariant: invalid requests have no observable state effect and retries cannot alter their original deadline.

Reservations.hold: build and validate the request/clock, then look up a receipt before reading current inventory/version. For a matching receipt return a detached copy of receipt.result; for any differing sku/count/expected/life throw. Invariant: identical idempotent retries return the original pending creation snapshot despite later activity and do not use retry now or current version.

Reservations.hold allocation: after no receipt exists, read the current item, reject missing/stale/insufficient requests before calling commit, calculate available-count and version+1 safely, then perform one commit containing item, pending hold, and original receipt. Invariant: successful allocation deducts once, increments SKU version once, records that creation version in Hold.version, and every failure leaves items/holds/receipts unchanged so the id is reusable.

Policy/Reservations terminal handling: allow pending -> confirmed/cancelled/expired only; return false only when the hold is already in the same requested terminal state, and throw for missing or a different terminal state. Confirmation commits only the hold state; cancellation and expiry add quantity to the current SKU availability and increment its current version exactly once. Invariant: no duplicate release, no opposite transition, and interleaved holds conserve inventory.

Reservations.expire: validate a nonnegative safe integer now, inspect only pending holds, and apply expired when expiresAt <= now. Do not invoke expiry from confirm/cancel and do not compare those operations to a wall clock. Invariant: expiry is inclusive, explicit, deterministic, and releases each eligible pending hold once.

Guard every computed inventory/version/deadline value used in a successful commit as a safe integer before commit. Invariant: allocation/release and version arithmetic stay safe while stock remains conserved.

Coordinator must independently verify every TASK.md acceptance requirement against all four modules, especially ownership: policy for validation/identity/arithmetic/transition calculation; service for ordering, atomic commit orchestration, and expiry semantics; store for deep detachment and snapshots; types for preserved exported shapes/signatures.
